subject: Clarifying temporary cache TTL and proof-of-removal for DPA appendix
messages:
From: Tara Nguyen <tara.nguyen@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: acme-security@example.com
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary cache TTL & DPA appendix questions

Ben — thanks for the quick demo last week. Security team has one remaining blocker before legal will push the DPA through: we need clearer language and an operational proof for short-lived caches (KV/prefix caching) that may contain customer inputs. Two asks: 1) a proposed definition and retention threshold for "temporary cache" in the DPA appendix and 2) an example of the deletion evidence we can expect (log sample, playbook).

Can you and your security/infra folks propose conservative TTLs and a sample proof-of-removal artifact we can share with our auditors? We don't need production data — a sanitized sample is fine.

Thanks,
Tara
Tara Nguyen
InfoSec Manager, Acme Retail

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Nguyen <tara.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Temporary cache TTL & DPA appendix questions

Tara — putting Mina and Olga on the thread; they own cache behavior and legal appendices on our side. High level answers up front: we treat ephemeral caches (model KV, prefix caches) as non-persistent, default TTL 72 hours, no snapshotting to backups, and immediate tombstoning on explicit erase requests. We can provide a sanitized deletion log and a short playbook describing how we drive the purge and verification.

Specifics we'll include:
- proposed DPA appendix language with a definition for "temporary cache" and explicit retention cap;
- a sample of the deletion audit log (hashed ids, timestamps, purge action ids);
- an outline of backup exception handling (if customer's workload has explicit on-demand history retention we surface that in the appendix).

Olga / Mina — can you prepare the sandboxed log sample and a 1-page playbook? Target: tomorrow EOD.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Tara Nguyen <tara.nguyen@acme.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Temporary cache TTL & DPA appendix questions

On Tue, Mar 16, 2027 at 10:03 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Tara — putting Mina and Olga on the thread; they own cache behavior and legal appendices on our side.

Tara — attaching a concise proposal inline below, plus a sanitized log sample attached as cache_snapshot_log.csv. Attachment includes: purge_timestamp, cache_key_hash, action_id, operator_id (redacted), verification_checksum. We replaced any customer-identifying content with stable hashes.

Proposed DPA appendix text (draft):
"Temporary Cache" means in-memory or local on-node key-value and prefix caches used to accelerate inference that by design do not persist to cold storage and are subject to a maximum retention period of 72 hours from creation, unless Customer elects a shorter retention in writing. Redwood will not include Temporary Cache contents in scheduled backups. On receipt of an Erasure Request, Redwood will purge affected Temporary Cache entries within 48 hours and provide a purge confirmation bundle including an audit action id and verification checksum.

Operational proof we can provide:
- Sanitized deletion audit (sample attached)
- Playbook: steps to trigger purge, background verification job, and publication of verification checksum to customer audit endpoint
- Timestamped snapshot of node-level cache clear events and the corresponding verification job results

Open items for legal/security review:
1) Does Acme require the purge SLA to be 24h vs 48h?
2) Are hashed keys acceptable proof, or do you need salted hashes with customer-specific salt?

I'll attach the one-pager playbook after a quick internal review.

Mina
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: cache_snapshot_log.csv (sanitized)

From: Tara Nguyen <tara.nguyen@acme.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: acme-security@example.com
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Temporary cache TTL & DPA appendix questions

Thanks Mina — helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- 48 hours for an Erasure Request is borderline for us; can you confirm whether 24 hours is technically feasible for typical discovery/erase flows? We're trying to minimize exposure windows.
- For proof: our auditors prefer salted hashes using a customer-supplied salt (so the hash can't be re-used across customers). Are you able to accept a customer-supplied salt per DPA?
- Can you also confirm whether the verification checksum will be posted to our audit webhook (we have a secure endpoint)?

If you can confirm these 3 items we can feed the appendix back to legal.

Tara

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Nguyen <tara.nguyen@acme.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Temporary cache TTL & DPA appendix questions

Tara — quick follow-up with answers after a brief infra feasibility check:
1) 24-hour purge SLA: technically feasible for most standard tenant flows provided there are no queued long-running batch jobs referencing the same caches. We can commit to 24 hours in the DPA appendix for Customer's production tenant, with an exception clause allowing longer purge windows during active incident remediation (with notification).
2) Salted hashes: yes — we can incorporate a customer-supplied salt for verification artifacts. We'll consume the salt as part of the audit-job input; salt will be stored in the customer's KMS key envelope and used only for generating verification artifacts.
3) Audit webhook: we can post the verification checksum and the purge action id to a customer-provided HTTPS endpoint (mutual TLS supported). We will include a signed timestamp (JWT) so Acme can validate integrity.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll attach the 1-page playbook and a redline of the proposed appendix into the DocuSign packet; Ben can coordinate the legal handoff.
- If Acme legal okays the 24h SLA + exception language + salt/webhook approach, we'll schedule a short technical sync to exchange the salt and webhook details.

Thanks,
Olga
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments: dpa_appendix_proof_template.pdf (draft appendix + playbook)
